absent: Inter processor handler internals for core sync, rseq, plain barrier and runqueue state updates.
Global expedited barrier path and architecture switch handling for membarrier.
Numeric values of membarrier commands, flags and state bits.
Full struct layouts and enum value encodings for psi states, task counts and aggregators.
Pressure record, poll, cgroup and filesystem interface behavior beyond trigger evaluation.

findings.text: System entry accepts a command plus flags plus target cpu and dispatches to query, global barrier, global expedited, private expedited variants with sync core and rseq options, registration helpers, and registration query, rejecting unknown commands and unexpected flags.

Private expedited registration moves from unregistered to pending to ready by setting a pending bit, propagating it to runqueues, then setting a ready bit; later expedited requests require the matching ready bit and fail with permission error otherwise, with distinct pairs for base, sync core and rseq flavors.

Private expedited execution validates build support and registration before doing work, returns success without cross cpu action when the address space has one user or the machine has one online cpu, except that the sync core flavor still needs local handling, and normalizes an absent target selector to broadcast.

Targeted expedited delivery ignores impossible or offline cpus, inspects the current task of the chosen cpu and only signals when that task belongs to the requesting address space; broadcast delivery builds a mask of online cpus whose current task belongs to that address space and then signals that mask.

Global query reports a fixed command mask but hides the non expedited global command when full tickless mode is enabled; the non expedited global command is rejected in that mode and otherwise waits for a grace period when more than one cpu is online.

Runqueue state propagation has a single user fast path that updates only the local runqueue state followed by a barrier, and a multi user path that waits for readers, collects matching cpus under locks, and synchronously updates their runqueue state before registration completes.

Registration query maps internal state bit pairs to command bits by testing grouped pending plus ready masks, accumulating corresponding command identifiers and clearing consumed bits, with an expectation that no unknown state bits remain.

Expedited and propagation paths serialize inter processor signalling, hold the cpu hotplug read lock while iterating online cpus, use read side critical sections to dereference per cpu current tasks, and pair caller side barriers with scheduler side ordering around current task changes.

Skipping the caller cpu is only safe for the plain barrier because migration ordering covers it; the sync core flavor must include the caller to avoid a thread in the same address space running without core synchronization after migration, while the rseq flavor must not disturb the caller because syscalls are forbidden inside rseq critical sections.

Early boot parameter handler parses a boolean string into a global enable flag controlling pressure stall monitoring, with a default enabled build and a default disabled build represented by two variants of the same flag.

System pressure group anchors per cpu storage for per cpu groups; per cpu group state observed includes accumulated per state times, a mask of active states, a start timestamp, task counters, and per aggregator previous snapshots used for delta computation.

Aggregation group state observed includes cumulative totals per aggregator, decaying averages and their totals, next and last average update times, an averages work item with its mutex, average and poll trigger lists, poll totals and poll scheduling controls.

Trigger state observed includes a monitored pressure state, a growth threshold, a time window with start time, start value, size and previous growth, plus pending flag, last event time, event cell, wait queue and optional filesystem object used for notification.

Per cpu pressure sampling takes a sequence protected coherent snapshot of clock, times, mask and start, folds currently active states up to now into the snapshot, then emits deltas against per aggregator previous values and records which states changed.

Collection over all possible cpus normalizes per cpu stall deltas by non idle weight to remove idle cpu artifacts, then integrates the normalized sample into cumulative totals; averages are updated on a fixed period schedule that accounts for missed periods and clock delay.

Averages worker folds per cpu times under the group averages mutex, refreshes triggers and averages when the next deadline has passed, and rearms itself on a jiffies delay only when recent activity indicates continued non idle work.

Trigger evaluation skips quiet triggers without pending events, updates a sliding window growth estimate with linear interpolation from the prior window, arms a pending breach when growth reaches threshold, rate limits signalling to once per window, and notifies either through filesystem notification or a wait queue.

Pressure readers use per cpu sequence counters with begin and retry around the snapshot; the averages worker serializes collection, trigger evaluation and average updates with the group averages mutex.

Lockless sampling can shift time into the following period and produce a sample larger than the period; the implementation clamps the integrated sample to the period and defers the excess rather than reporting above full pressure or dropping it.

Averages worker restart logic treats the worker cpu specially because the worker itself keeps that cpu non idle, using task counters there and non idle deltas elsewhere to decide whether rescheduling is required.
Pressure sampling period uses a frequency of two seconds plus one tick, with fixed point decay factors for ten second, sixty second and three hundred second averages.
Trigger windows are bounded by a maximum size of ten seconds expressed in microseconds and an update density of ten updates per window.
Load tracking defines a minimum divider derived from the maximum average minus one thousand twenty four.
Pressure subsystem has a global bug indicator, a disabled static key defaulting false, a cgroups enabled static key defaulting true, and a period variable shared across groups.
